findings.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:6` imports `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` from `"../throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam"` (i.e. `packages/app-store/_utils/throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam.ts`). That file does not exist anywhere in the repo (`find . -iname "*throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam*"` returns nothing). Every non-team OAuth credential creation path calls this function — hubspot, salesforce, office365calendar/video, larkcalendar, zoho-bigin all import `createOAuthAppCredential` from this file (see `packages/app-store/hubspot/api/callback.ts:11`, `packages/app-store/salesforce/api/callback.ts:10`). This will fail TypeScript compilation and break every OAuth app installation flow for a normal (non-team) user.
**`minimumTokenResponseSchema` is broken and silently strips required fields when credential sync is enabled.**

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10` uses computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Since Zod schema objects don't override `toString()`, both evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"` — not a dynamic "any numeric key" matcher as apparently intended. The second key overwrites the first in the object literal, so the effective schema is just `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`. Because `z.object()` strips unrecognized keys by default, `refreshTokenResponse.data` will only ever contain `access_token` (plus the dead `"[object Object]"` key) — all other fields (`expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, `instance_url`, etc.) are dropped. This directly feeds credential persistence: `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:90-96` does `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and saves the result to `prisma.credential.update`. With credential sync enabled this will corrupt/erase calendar credentials (losing `expiry_date`), silently breaking token refresh for every app that uses this helper.
**Inconsistent return type from `refreshOAuthTokens` breaks Google Calendar and Hubspot refresh when sync is enabled.**
`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6-12`: when sync is enabled, it returns the raw `fetch` `Response`; when disabled, it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` resolves to.

Google: `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-91` — the non-sync branch returns `fetchTokens.res` (a google-auth-library response with `.data`), but the sync branch returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, which has no `.data` property. `const token = res?.data` will be `undefined` when sync is enabled, and `googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` will throw (`Cannot read properties of undefined`).

Hubspot: `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-188` — non-sync branch returns an already-parsed `HubspotToken` object from the HubSpot SDK; sync branch returns a raw `fetch` Response assigned to the same `HubspotToken`-typed variable, so downstream field access (e.g. `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token`, expiry math) will read `undefined` off the Response object.
**Webhook endpoint has no rate limiting / timing-safe comparison, and will throw an uncaught error on malformed/decrypt-failure input.**

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:20-24` compares the secret with `!==`, which is not constant-time and is vulnerable to timing attacks for a security-critical shared secret. More importantly, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 26) and `symmetricDecrypt(...)` (line 47-49) are not wrapped in try/catch — a malformed body or an undecryptable `keys` payload will throw an unhandled exception, and since there's no try/catch around the handler, Next.js will return a raw 500 with a stack trace (or crash the request) rather than a clean 400. This is an externally-reachable webhook endpoint (self-hosters point their apps at it), so it needs input validation error handling.
**`CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` unset falls back to `""`, which will make `symmetricDecrypt` fail unpredictably instead of failing closed with a clear error.**

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:47-49`: `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""`. If the operator enabled `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and set the webhook secret but forgot the encryption key, this silently attempts AES with an empty key rather than failing with an actionable error at startup or with a clear 500 message.
**`salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-104`: refresh-and-persist logic runs unconditionally on every `getClient()`/connection call, not just when the token is actually expired.**
**`refreshOAuthTokens` swallows non-2xx responses from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without validation.**

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16` returns the raw fetch `Response` regardless of `response.ok`. Callers generally rely on `handleErrorsJson`/`handleWebexResponse`/etc. to catch failures, but not all paths do this consistently (e.g. Google's flow does `res?.data` directly with no status check at all — see issue 3).

**`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:39-40`** looks up the app by `slug: reqBody.appSlug`, but then re-looks up `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` — this is a needless double lookup since `app.slug === reqBody.appSlug` by construction of the query; minor but adds an unnecessary DB round trip layer of indirection for something already validated.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts` and `decodeOAuthState.ts` are functionally identical (both parse `req.query.state`; "encode" then re-stringifies what it just parsed). This is pre-existing naming confusion carried over from the previous location, not introduced by this diff, but since the PR touches these files it would have been a good opportunity to fix/rename (`encodeOAuthState` doesn't actually encode a state object passed in by the caller — it just round-trips the query string).

No automated tests were added for `createOAuthAppCredential`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`, or the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint — given these are security/credential-handling code paths, at least unit tests for the schema validation and webhook auth/decrypt failure modes would materially reduce risk here (and likely would have caught issues #2 and #3).
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:14` — stray empty JSDoc comment `/** */` above the handler; dead/no-op comment, remove.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`minimumTokenResponseSchema` is broken and silently strips required fields when credential sync is enabled.**

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is intended to accept `access_token` plus “any numeric expiry field” and other properties when credential sync is enabled. But the schema is incorrectly written:

```ts
[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),
[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),
```

In a JS object literal, those computed keys evaluate to literal strings (e.g., `z.string().toString()` becomes something like `"ZodString"`), so this does not create a dynamic catchall. Instead it defines (and even overwrites) a single fixed property key, and Zod `z.object(...)` will *strip all unknown keys by default*. As a result, when credential sync is enabled, responses like `{ access_token, expires_in }` will parse successfully but `expires_in`/`expiry_date` (or any other required fields) will be removed from `.data`, i.e., “silently stripped”. This is a real, verifiable correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10` uses computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Since Zod schema objects don't override `toString()`, both evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"` — not a dynamic "any numeric key" matcher as apparently intended. The second key overwrites the first in the object literal, so the effective schema is just `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`. Because `z.object()` strips unrecognized keys by default, `refreshTokenResponse.data` will only ever contain `access_token` (plus the dead `"[object Object]"` key) — all other fields (`expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, `instance_url`, etc.) are dropped. This directly feeds credential persistence: `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:90-96` does `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and saves the result to `prisma.credential.update`. With credential sync enabled this will corrupt/erase calendar credentials (losing `expiry_date`), silently breaking token refresh for every app that uses this helper.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the object literal uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those are evaluated immediately to a fixed string (not an index-signature / dynamic key matcher), and the second overwrites the first, so the schema does not actually accept/retain arbitrary numeric expiry fields. Also, `z.object()` will strip unknown keys by default, so even a successful parse will drop fields like `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc. With credential sync enabled, the function switches to this minimum schema, and callers like `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` then persist the parsed result; this can effectively erase important credential fields (and in Google’s case they assign the SafeParse result to `key`), breaking token refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` unset falls back to `""`, which will make `symmetricDecrypt` fail unpredictably instead of failing closed with a clear error.**

adjudication.rationale:
In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, decryption is done with:
```ts
symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")
```
If `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset/misconfigured, the code silently substitutes an empty string key and proceeds to `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)`. There is no explicit validation or clear error response for a missing key, so requests will likely fail via thrown exceptions (500) or otherwise behave inconsistently depending on `symmetricDecrypt`’s implementation, rather than failing closed with a controlled, explicit error. This is directly present in the diff and is a real correctness/robustness issue introduced by the fallback to `""`.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` using `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` and then immediately `JSON.parse(...)`. There is no validation that `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set when the endpoint is enabled/used. If it’s missing, the code will still attempt decryption with an empty-string key, leading to non-obvious runtime failures (e.g., decrypt/JSON.parse throwing) rather than a clear configuration error response. This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`refreshOAuthTokens` swallows non-2xx responses from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without validation.**

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function does `const response = await fetch(...)` and immediately `return response;` without checking `response.ok` / status code or parsing/validating the body. That means non-2xx responses from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are not validated at this layer and are passed through to callers. Some callers may handle errors later (e.g., `handleErrorsJson`), but others (e.g., Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object) do not validate the returned `Response` and would not detect non-2xx in a controlled way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16` returns the raw fetch `Response` regardless of `response.ok`. Callers generally rely on `handleErrorsJson`/`handleWebexResponse`/etc. to catch failures, but not all paths do this consistently (e.g. Google's flow does `res?.data` directly with no status check at all — see issue 3).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` the credential-sync branch does `const response = await fetch(...); return response;` without checking `response.ok` or parsing/normalizing the body. This is verifiably problematic given callers’ expectations: e.g. in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assumes the returned object has `res?.data` (`const token = res?.data;`) which matches the old Google auth refresh flow, but if the sync endpoint is used the returned value is a WHATWG `Response` (no `.data`), so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw. Even aside from that mismatch, returning an unchecked raw `Response` means errors may slip through unless every caller consistently runs `handleErrorsJson`/similar, which is not true in the Google path shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:39-40`** looks up the app by `slug: reqBody.appSlug`, but then re-looks up `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` — this is a needless double lookup since `app.slug === reqBody.appSlug` by construction of the query; minor but adds an unnecessary DB round trip layer of indirection for something already validated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows only one DB query for the app: `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug }, select: { slug: true } })`. The subsequent `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` is an in-memory lookup, not another DB round trip. Also, `reqBody.appSlug` is only validated as a string by zod; the DB lookup is the first actual existence check for that slug. So the finding mischaracterizes this as a redundant/double DB lookup and as something “already validated.” At most, using `reqBody.appSlug` instead of `app.slug` would be a trivial simplification, not a clear defect.
